definition: In this biological context, aberration refers to an optical irregularity of the cornea measured as a wavefront distortion. Higher aberration values indicate a departure from normal light focusing and can be associated with poorer objective visual quality.

reasons: The packet does not provide a definition stating that “aberration” refers to an “optical irregularity of the cornea measured as a wavefront distortion.” It only reports that “corneal wavefront aberrations” were measured using the Pentacam system.
The claim that “Higher aberration values indicate a departure from normal light focusing” is not explicitly supported in the packet.

The claim that higher aberration values “can be associated with poorer objective visual quality” is not directly established as a general rule in the packet; it reports specific longitudinal changes (e.g., OSI increased, SR decreased) and changes in aberration RMS values, but does not support the causal/interpretive linkage as stated.
The definition is written as a general interpretation rather than something the packet explicitly defines for this term.

The packet supports corneal wavefront aberrations and their association with objective visual quality, but it does not explicitly support defining aberration as a corneal optical irregularity measured as a wavefront distortion.
The phrase "departure from normal light focusing" is an added explanatory gloss not stated in the source packet.
The packet supports an association between increased aberration values and worse objective visual quality, but not the broader definitional claims as written.
